claims.statement: The 2002 study groups the city into three characteristic zones with a design spectrum each.
Zone A is ash, Zone B is fill, Zone C is rock, flows and thin deposits.
Figura 8.5 prints To, Tc, TL, Am, An, Fa and Fv for each of the three zones.
The published design spectra are for 5% of critical damping at ground surface.
The parameter sheet itself is labelled 5% of critical damping.
The recommendations complement the national code and no requirement may be taken below it — which is why the importance coefficient still multiplies the ordinate.
The user-supplied importance factor follows the national table of importance coefficients.
The entrance branch below To is printed on Figura 8.1.
The descending branch is Sa = An·Fv/T.
Beyond TL the sheet prints a constant floor Sa = Am/2.
To, Tc and TL are the printed abscissae that separate the branches.
Structures with a fundamental period at or above 2.0 s require special seismic analyses.
Using the Zone C spectra must be explicitly justified by the geotechnical engineer.
Sites near slope crests must additionally apply the topographic amplification factors, which this engine does not compute.
The study complements the NSR-98 corpus and no municipal adoption or extension act was located, so its currency is warned rather than asserted.
Manizales remains in a high seismic hazard zone for complementary code requirements.
Am is the ground-surface equivalent of the national Aa coefficient.
When the zone is in doubt the study directs the engineer to use Zone A.
